title: Reduce repeated test work and run two grouped workers
body:
The test suite repeatedly rebuilds equivalent verification inputs and recalculates identical independent reference results. This branch shares those observations and reference calculations, consolidates duplicate checks, and runs two grouped test workers. Scientific runtime, numerical tolerances, distinct failure checks, and genuine reader timeout tests are preserved.

On one local before/after pair, full verification fell from **61 min 06.65 s to 20 min 29.67 s**. The runs had different background load and cache histories; this is an observed improvement, not a controlled benchmark.

**Draft: integration with current main is unresolved.** This branch was developed and verified from the pre-C-equivalence baseline. Current `main` has since retired many of the scientific tests changed here. A read-only merge projection found **17 conflicting paths**: four content conflicts and 13 modify/delete conflicts. The exact tested branch is published unchanged for review. Relevant improvements need to be reconciled with the rebuilt suite before merge; retired scientific tests must not be restored simply to resolve conflicts.

<details>
<summary>Technical appendix: implementation and validation</summary>

### Scope and implementation

- Remove 163 repeated fixed-profile verifier acquisitions (260 → 97), while retaining live output-collision challenges and separate mutable copies.
- Reuse exact independent numerical and optical reference results with immutable cached values, fresh returned arrays, and fallback for unsupported diagnostic contexts.
- Consolidate equivalent assertions into stronger public-entry checks. Account for all 1,902 original declarations: 1,843 retain, 57 consolidate, two repair; add three supplemental reference-cache proof declarations. All 18 removed declaration names have keeper mappings.
- Qualify two pytest workers using `-n 2 --dist loadgroup --max-worker-restart 0`. Preserve shared reader-cache affinity, nested serial selectors, native worker/subprocess coverage, omission failures and crash handling.
- Pin only the new development dependencies `pytest-xdist==3.8.0` and `execnet==2.1.2`.
- Keep the genuine 180 s parent deadline and 15 s socket timeout, both full noisy-study geometries, and the original phase-estimation test file.
- Scientific runtime and contracts are unchanged. The only changed runtime-package file is the pytest infrastructure module.
- The diff is 25 files, 1,322 insertions and 522 deletions. Shared fixtures, isolation proofs and documentation add code while repeated execution decreases.

The tracked task contract is `docs/tasks/test-efficiency-audit.md`. PR #56 supplied comparison evidence; its scientific baseline and shortened deadline were not imported.

| Tested/published head | `d9b2d9e108b9b23c087a9daadfbeb54b17b4d17e` |
| Tested tree | `1c128102e30279dae75304d0bdbfad17677d74f5` |

Fresh blind test reviews accepted the final checkpoints. Restricted verification role C passed the exact candidate. Fresh independent scientific review D accepted the declared preservation scope and final declaration audit; a separate fresh bounded reviewer accepted the five infrastructure paths and passing candidate. These verdicts apply to the tested head, not an integration with newer main.

All 733 tracked file hashes and 188 final evidence pins were rechecked after cleanup and before publication. The branch is clean. Tool/executable hashes, dependency lock and retained receipt inputs still match the completed run. Push-time lint and format checks also passed.

### Verification and observed performance

Canonical `make verify` exited 0; all 13 phases passed on macOS 27.0.1 arm64 with project Python 3.13.12, uv 0.12.19 and Java 21.0.7. Verification context was `TEST-EFFICIENCY`, reviewed tests equal to the head above, and integration base equal to the tested baseline above. The exact original invocation, private executable paths, environment and logs are retained locally.

| Measurement | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Complete gate wall time | 3,666.65 s | 1,229.67 s |
| Pytest wall time | 3,392.25 s | 1,185.32 s |
| Passed cases | 11,299 | 11,225 |
| Skipped cases | 0 | 0 |

The candidate reported 29 warnings. Parallel per-file durations overlap and cannot be summed as elapsed time. Both timing runs were contended. Test counts and measured coverage do not establish complete behavioral correctness.

Native coverage includes all 58 owned Python files and measured subprocesses, with zero excluded lines:

| Scope | Files | Covered/total executable statements | Covered/total branch destinations |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Global | 58 | 7,724 / 8,011 | 2,231 / 2,380 |
| Runtime package | 44 | 3,534 / 3,535 | 987 / 988 |
| Delivery scripts | 14 | 4,190 / 4,476 | 1,244 / 1,392 |

Percentages are advisory under the inherited policy. Native measurement/report and omission gates remain binding. Separate language-level statement coverage and native dependency internals are unmeasured.

The same-run memory measurement was 112,852,992 B peak minus 97,632,256 B baseline = **15,220,736 B**, below the **33,554,432 B** limit. The wheel and isolated import passed; locked dependency audit found no known vulnerabilities or adverse statuses in 28 packages at verification time.

Wheel: `simrecon-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl`, 123,334 B, SHA-256 `463792122ef5b1345d1d094a28e65679de0178cbc3606ad1f70a0e742c6825b6`. All 44 package source members match the tested candidate. The build/import commands did not emit a complete resolved transitive environment or isolated-interpreter manifest; those provenance limits remain.

Configured Ubuntu 24.04 and macOS 15 continuous integration has not been validated for this PR. The 17 merge conflicts also leave integration with the current main unverified. This is not a merge or release readiness claim.

### Retained evidence and cleanup

Detailed run logs, checkpoint mappings, independent verdicts, timing records and cumulative accounting are retained locally in the ignored `artifacts/test-efficiency/` directory; they are not tracked GitHub attachments. Selected evidence fingerprints:

- Canonical receipt: `80e41576ad575e410ed55ebe4f67e7363fe83599b509a64607cb57a96fa341c1`
- C verification handoff: `b54b6bd4e528471e15d29167f2e950b0e817b1c8988812696bedabd802d50792`
- D final verdict: `327a8a558b4d600afc97fe58d439795eb2707a46934468625bdeb6727c686ddc`
- Bounded final verdict: `a8459baed91f33466b27b93d9c385757b742da1c64128bbc33dda7b58c469b59`

Two independently reviewed cleanup operations removed 1,407 positively identified disposable units, representing 2,346,082,304 allocated bytes before removal. Original evidence, links and required referents/ancestors, environments, real caches and backups passed independent preservation checks. Filesystem free-space recovery was not measured.

No human numeric budget was set. Earlier reviews, corrections and the abandoned low-value phase cache remain in cumulative accounting; actual served-model attribution, root/collaboration usage and monetary cost are unknown. No merge or release is authorized by this publication request.

</details>
